age-structure.def: A graph of how many people (or what percent of a population) are in each age group, usually with males on the left and females on the right and the youngest at the bottom. Also called a population pyramid. Its shape predicts whether a population will grow, stay stable or shrink.

cohort.def: A group of people born during the same span of years, shown as one bar of an age structure diagram, such as everyone aged 0 to 9.

population-momentum.def: The tendency of a population with many young people to keep growing for decades even after families have fewer children, because the large young cohorts are still reaching the ages when people have children.

development-level.def: A developed country has a high average income, widespread schooling and health care, and usually slow population growth; a developing country has a lower average income and usually a younger, faster-growing population.
